docs.title: Loki runtime retention is verifiable via the retention_hours metric label
docs.content:
# Loki runtime retention is verifiable via the retention_hours metric label

When changing `limits_config.retention_period` in `/etc/loki/config.yaml` and restarting `loki.service`, the cleanest way to confirm the new value is honored at runtime (not just present in the file) is to scrape `/metrics` and inspect the `retention_hours="..."` label on `loki_distributor_bytes_received_total`. Loki stamps the **runtime-effective** retention onto this metric label as hours. So `retention_hours="2160"` confirms 90d × 24h = 2160h is in force.

Curl this:
```bash
curl -sS http://127.0.0.1:3100/metrics | grep loki_distributor_bytes_received_total
```

Output excerpt:
```
loki_distributor_bytes_received_total{aggregated_metric="false",retention_hours="2160",tenant="fake"} 58154
```

The `/config` endpoint also reflects the new value (`retention_period: 90d` under `limits_config`), but `/config` shows the parsed YAML — it does not prove Loki has wired retention into its enforcement loop. The metric label proves both.

Also note: `/config` shows TWO `retention_period` keys in output: one under `limits_config` (the global retention you care about) and one under `compactor` (per-stream override default, value `0s`, normal/expected). Don't be alarmed by the second one.

Discovered 2026-05-09 during Layer 1 retention bump from 30d → 90d.

docs.title: Stargate has no Prometheus / node_exporter; only Loki as a Grafana datasource
docs.content:
# Stargate has no Prometheus / node_exporter; only Loki as a Grafana datasource

Discovered 2026-05-09: stargate runs `grafana-server.service` and `loki.service`, but no `prometheus`, no `node_exporter`, no `alloy`/`grafana-agent`/`promtail`. The only configured Grafana datasource is Loki (UID `ffiyv6uwwds74d`). All existing Grafana alert rules in `/etc/grafana/provisioning/alerting/nimbus-alert-rules.yaml` execute as Loki queries, not Prometheus queries.

Implication: any "Grafana alert on filesystem / CPU / memory / network" requires deploying Prometheus + node_exporter first. There is no metrics datasource today. Don't propose Grafana metrics-based alerts in plans without confirming this is fixed.

Workarounds available today without a metrics stack:
- Email-only alerts via `msmtp` + a systemd timer running a shell check (see `nimbus-healthcheck.timer` for the pattern).
- Logging the `df` output to syslog and alerting via Loki query (requires a log shipper on stargate, which also doesn't exist).

Proper fix tracked as a separate backlog item: deploy node_exporter + Prometheus on stargate. Filed 2026-05-09 alongside this learning.

Existing observability components on stargate:
- `grafana-server` (port 3000)
- `loki` (port 3100, single-tenant, filesystem storage)
- `nimbus-healthcheck.timer` (every 5min, custom)
- `mysql-backup-push-verify.timer`, `mysql-backup-verify.timer`, `mysql-backup-push-retry.timer`
- `msmtp` + `msmtp-mta` for outbound email

Missing:
- node_exporter, Prometheus, log shipper (promtail/alloy)

docs.title: Pair-flow Child B shipped: PairMeural REJECT + BridgeStatusHandler self-heal backfill
docs.content:
# Pair-flow Child B shipped: PairMeural REJECT + BridgeStatusHandler self-heal backfill

2026-05-09: closed `backlog_a589828915b8` (Child B of fb6f9da611e8). Fix has two complementary parts; together they obsolete the manual-stitch recipe.

**Part 1: BridgeController.PairMeural REJECT semantic** (`BridgeController.cs:746`).
After `GetByHWIdAsync(meuralHwId)` returns an existing Frame, check `existingFrame.BridgeHwId`. If set AND ≠ this bridge's HwId, return `409 MEURAL_ALREADY_PAIRED` with no state change. The orphan-adoption path (BridgeHwId IS NULL) is unchanged — needed for the self-heal scenarios where auto-provision created the Frame without a bridge link. No transfer-ownership semantics, per Tom's 2026-05-08 decision.

**Part 2: BridgeStatusHandler.BackfillFrameStitch** (`BridgeStatusHandler.cs:230`).
Runs on every non-retained `bridge/+/status`. For each `MeuralInfo` in `status.meurals[]` with a `frameUuid`:
1. Look up Frame and the FrameHW that points at it (reverse half-link from auto-provision) in one JOIN.
2. If `Frame.BridgeHwId IS NULL` → set to this bridge's HwId (looked up by `Bridges.Unique = bridgeUuid`).
3. If `Frame.HWId IS NULL` AND `FrameHW.FrameId = Frame.Id` reverse-link exists → set `Frame.HWId = FrameHW.Id`.
4. Drift case (`Frame.BridgeHwId` already set to a *different* bridge): log a `[BridgeStatusHandler] Backfill DRIFT` warning, do not overwrite. PairMeural REJECT prevents legitimate transfers, so any drift here is data corruption to be triaged by a human.

Idempotent — once stitched, subsequent statuses are no-ops. Cheap (one JOIN per Meural per status). Skipped during the 10-second retained-replay window already in BridgeStatusHandler.

**Why this approach over alternatives:**
- "Refuse auto-provision for productId=21" would have required a frames-team contract change to handle the rejection on the bridge JVM side. Higher coordination cost; doesn't self-heal existing orphans.
- "Add bridgeUuid to MQTT provision request" — same issue, coordination + doesn't self-heal.
- Backfill via status: zero contract change, self-heals on next status, idempotent, cheap.

**Why ProvisionNewFrame's half-link is intentional, not a bug to fix.**
`FrameProvisioningService.ProvisionNewFrame` writes `FrameHW.FrameId = frameId` (line 345) but does NOT write `Frame.HWId = hwId`. This was originally a gap, but with the new backfill the half-link is sufficient: the backfill uses the FrameHW->Frame back-link to derive HWId on the next status. Avoiding a fix in ProvisionNewFrame keeps the auto-provision path simple and reduces transactional surface; the backfill cleans up.

**Verification.**
- Deployed to abydos 2026-05-09. New strings in DLLs confirmed: `Backfill: Frame`, `Backfill DRIFT` in NimbusCommon.dll; `MEURAL_ALREADY_PAIRED` in picFrameWeb.dll.
- DB sweep: only one Meural-bridge frame currently has NULL BridgeHwId (`Frame 603` warhol-757 duplicate, soft-tombstoned via `Flags=16`). Its `Unique` differs from Frame 610's, so bridge status doesn't reference it; backfill correctly skips.
- BridgeStatusHandler is processing live status messages post-deploy without errors; backfill is silent (no orphans to stitch).

**Backlog `backlog_418379339f3b` Option 3 (NimbusService Frame_Publisher disconnect cleanup) is still open** as the remaining hygiene item from the retained-replay work earlier this session.

docs.title: Redis bridge:<uuid>:data uses alias and frameUuid for Meurals (not name/unique)
docs.content:
# Redis bridge:<uuid>:data uses alias and frameUuid for Meurals (not name/unique)

The per-bridge Redis JSON at key `bridge:<bridges.Unique>:data` has a `meurals` array where each entry uses these field names:

- `alias` — Meural display name (e.g., "warhol-757", "renoir-33"). NOT `name`.
- `frameUuid` — equals `picFrame.Frames.Unique`. NOT `unique`. **This is the value to use in `frame/{uuid}/commands` MQTT topics** (matches `mqtt:frame-clear-media-cache` v1.0.1 spec semantics).
- `ip` — Meural's LAN IP
- `lastSeen` — epoch seconds (last successful agent→Meural probe)
- `reachable` — bool

Top-level fields on the bridge data:
- `picFrameVersion` — actual running picFrame jar version (canonical for OTA verification — DB SwVersion lags)
- `version` — agent version
- `meuralCount`, `online`, `localIP`, `wifiSSID`, `wifiSignal`, `cpuTemp`, `uptime` (sec since agent start), `systemUptime` (sec since boot), `model`, `osVersion`, `platform`, `uuid` (= bridges.Unique)

Use case: enumerating Meurals for a fleet-wide MQTT fanout (e.g., clearMediaCache after upgrade) is a one-stop Redis lookup per bridge — no SQL JOIN to picFrame.frames needed. Faster than DB and reflects authoritative agent-side state.

Discovered 2026-05-09 while fanning out clearMediaCache after Wave 2/3 OTA promote. Initial Python parse with `m.get("name")` / `m.get("unique")` returned all nulls; raw GET revealed actual field names.

docs.title: frame_config.json.backup is the bench/clean recovery escape hatch when registration is rate-limited
docs.content:
# frame_config.json.backup is the bench/clean recovery escape hatch when registration is rate-limited

When a bench cleanup leaves a Meural's `/usr/local/bin/meurals/<uuid>/frame_config.json` stripped to its minimal form (mqttBroker, mqttPassword, mqttUsername, serverUrl, unique only — no `ip`, `name`, `serialNumber`), the supervisor.go path skips JVM spawn and waits for the network-scan/register flow to repopulate. If `/api/device/register` returns 429 (server-side rate limit), the bench can sit stuck with no JVM, no MQTT subscriber, and the frame appears offline in the UI — even after the Redis-side rate limit clears, because reconcileMeurals only fires on CloudMQTT config-receive events.

**Recovery technique:** restore from the per-Meural `frame_config.json.backup` file in the same directory:
```
cp /usr/local/bin/meurals/<uuid>/frame_config.json.backup \
   /usr/local/bin/meurals/<uuid>/frame_config.json
```

The `.backup` file is written by the agent post-discovery and contains the full populated config (`ip`, `name`, `serialNumber`, plus the standard mqtt/server fields). Once restored, supervisor.go's per-minute pickup loop sees IP populated within ~60s and spawns the JVM directly, bypassing the rate-limited register API entirely.

This is the right fix when:
- Bench was just cleaned and the agent never successfully registered post-clean
- You hit the rate limit during debugging churn (orphan agent, repeated systemctl restarts, etc.)
- You need the bench back NOW and don't want to wait for the rate-limit window to clear

Used 2026-05-09 to recover .47 bench after my orphan-agent probe induced a server-side rate limit on MEU1118020008094. JVM spawned within ~70s of the restore.

Becomes less critical once nimbus-agent 1.15.10 ships (typed ErrRateLimited + 5-min reconcile ticker self-heal), but the .backup file remains useful for forced-recovery scenarios where waiting isn't acceptable.

docs.content:
# Audit triggers shipped on accounting + artwork — trigger count 11 → 23 on stargate

2026-05-09: closed `backlog_8b725d0e893e` (Phase 0 ship blocker). Mirrors the picframe audit pattern onto money-adjacent tables.

**Live state on stargate:**
- Trigger count by schema: `picframe=11, accounting=6, artwork=6` (was 11, 0, 0).
- New audit shadow tables (all `_audit` suffix, lowercase per `lower_case_table_names=1`):
  - `accounting.servicev2_audit`, `accounting.sales_audit`, `accounting.invoices_audit`
  - `artwork.subscriptions_audit`, `artwork.artpurchases_audit`, `artwork.billingaccount_audit`
- Each shadow has shape: `AuditId INT PK auto_inc, Action VARCHAR(10), RecordId INT, OldValues LONGTEXT (JSON), DeletedBy VARCHAR(128), DeletedAt DATETIME(6), AppName VARCHAR(128)` + `IX_*_RecordId` + `IX_*_DeletedAt`.
- 12 new triggers (UPDATE + DELETE pair on each source table). Trigger naming: `TR_<TableCamel>_AuditUpdate` / `TR_<TableCamel>_AuditDelete`.

**Decisions:**
- **No redaction** (Tom-approved 2026-05-09). Match the picframe policy exactly: OldValues stored verbatim. Sensitive payment-provider columns (`accounting.sales.cart`, `accounting.invoices.invoiceJson`, `artwork.billingaccount.details`) are NOT redacted because audit value is recovery, and recovery requires the full row. If a future compliance review requires redaction, it's a separate change.
- **No `*_audit` self-trigger.** Audit tables are not audited. Deletes from audit tables (e.g., manual cleanup) leave no trace by design.

**Verification:** transactional probe — `BEGIN; UPDATE accounting.sales SET DateUpdated=DateUpdated WHERE Id=10010; SELECT FROM accounting.sales_audit; ROLLBACK;` showed the trigger fired (AuditId=1 within txn), and ROLLBACK correctly rolled back both the parent UPDATE and the trigger's audit INSERT (post-rollback count=0). Production unchanged.

**Scope skipped** (per backlog rationale):
- `accounting.service` — being dropped post-migration.
- `accounting.usercredits` — descoped per no-credit rule.
- `accounting.coupon`, `accounting.payable`, `accounting.paymentmethods`, `accounting.servicegroups`, `accounting.servicetype`, `accounting.amazonpaymentdetails`, `accounting.shopify`, `accounting.woocommerce` — not Phase 0 ship-critical.

**Coordination:** sent infra-team a heads-up (msg_<id>) — `audit-health-check.sh` asserts `trigger count=11` and will fail tonight's 03:00 UTC run if not updated to expect 23.

**Source of truth:** DDL captured in `picFrameWeb/create-triggers-payments.sql` (committed master). Idempotent: `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` + `DROP TRIGGER IF EXISTS`. Safe to re-apply after future NimbusSync full-resyncs (which strip triggers and indexes).

**Future re-capture command:** `ssh ubuntu@stargate "sudo mysqldump --no-defaults -u root --no-data --no-create-info --no-create-db --triggers --skip-comments --skip-add-drop-table accounting artwork" > picFrameWeb/create-triggers-payments.sql.recapture` — but mysqldump doesn't emit the audit tables themselves, so the CREATE TABLE blocks at the top of the canonical file are hand-maintained.

docs.title: picFrame.Frames audit triggers had pre-existing BridgeHwId gap (fixed 2026-05-09)
docs.content:
# picFrame.Frames audit triggers had pre-existing BridgeHwId gap (fixed 2026-05-09)

Both `TR_Frames_AuditUpdate` and `TR_Frames_AuditDelete` (created 2026-04-20) used an EXPLICIT JSON_OBJECT column list and were missing **BridgeHwId** (column #35 of `picFrame.Frames`). This meant any UPDATE/DELETE that nulled BridgeHwId — most notably `BridgeController.CleanupMeuralFrame`'s unpair UPDATE at BridgeController.cs:1815 — was silently un-audited for that field. The audit row captured uId/HWId being nulled but not BridgeHwId, making un-stitch operations partially invisible in the audit trail.

Discovered 2026-05-09 while doing Child D (LastUnpairedAt). Fixed in same migration (`picFrameWeb/add-LastUnpairedAt-frames.sql`) by recreating both triggers to include BridgeHwId AND LastUnpairedAt in the JSON_OBJECT.

When auditing other tables that use this JSON_OBJECT-explicit-list pattern, verify the column list against current schema. Audit triggers can drift silently when columns are added without trigger updates.

docs.title: MySQL 8.0.45 does NOT support `ALTER TABLE … ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS`
docs.content:
# MySQL 8.0.45 does NOT support `ALTER TABLE … ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS`

Despite frequent statements in MySQL community docs that 8.0.29+ supports `ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS`, stargate's MySQL 8.0.45-0ubuntu0.24.04.1 hard-errors with `You have an error in your SQL syntax; ... near 'IF NOT EXISTS <colname> ...'`. The `IF NOT EXISTS` clause is supported on `CREATE TABLE`, `CREATE INDEX`, `CREATE TRIGGER` (DROP, in our triggers file), but NOT on `ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN`.

Idempotent workaround:
```sql
SET @col_exists = (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM information_schema.COLUMNS
                   WHERE TABLE_SCHEMA='picFrame' AND TABLE_NAME='Frames'
                     AND COLUMN_NAME='LastUnpairedAt');
SET @sql = IF(@col_exists = 0,
              'ALTER TABLE picFrame.Frames ADD COLUMN LastUnpairedAt DATETIME NULL AFTER BridgeHwId',
              'DO 0');
PREPARE stmt FROM @sql; EXECUTE stmt; DEALLOCATE PREPARE stmt;
```

Use this pattern for all idempotent column-add migrations against stargate. See `picFrameWeb/add-LastUnpairedAt-frames.sql` for canonical example.

docs.title: Frame visual monitor ground-truth: subscribe to frame/+/status and diff currentMedia
docs.content:
# Frame visual monitor ground-truth: subscribe to frame/+/status and diff currentMedia

For the tools:frame-visual-monitor side-tool, the cleanest "bridge pushed an image" signal is to subscribe to `frame/+/status` (retained, QoS 1) and watch the `currentMedia` field per frame UUID. A change in `currentMedia` for a given UUID = a real push event happened. Filter out `source: "server"` messages — those are server-published retained snapshots intended for mobile clients on subscribe, would cause feedback loops if treated as bridge push events.

Why this works without needing a new publish on the bridge side:
- The per-Meural picFrameClient JVM (running inside the bridge process in headless mode) publishes status with currentMedia
- MqttStatusHandler.HandleStatusMessage on the server already does media-id-change detection on this exact topic — proves it's a reliable signal source
- Server's MqttToSignalRBridge has a "media-id-changed debounce" referenced in its gotchas

Why NOT to subscribe to frame/+/changed instead:
- It's a server-internal fanout topic — derivative of MqttStatusHandler processing, not the source of truth
- Adding the watcher as another consumer of /changed couples it to server-team's debounce logic

The 45s rePushTimer in MeuralDisplay.displayImage does HTTP POSTs (not MQTT) and re-pushes the SAME image to beat the Meural's ~60s postcard expiry. This means `currentMedia` should NOT move on each rePush (still pending frames-team confirmation). Implication for the monitor's stuck_image alert rule: the bridge can be doing real work continuously even when both visual content and currentMedia stay constant. Don't treat "no change for >X" as anomaly without comparing against the configured rotation_interval_seconds.

Pending confirmation from frames-team (msg sent 2026-05-09): cadence (event-driven vs heartbeat), currentMedia set-after-success vs optimistic, and whether frame/+/imageChange is dead code or a separate publisher.

docs.title: requestArtAccess.aa.width/height are bridge orient-lock filter input, NOT MP4 container dims
docs.content:
# requestArtAccess.aa.width/height are bridge orient-lock filter input, NOT MP4 container dims

FrameController.cs:815 `requestArtAccess` returns an `ArtAccess` struct with `width`/`height` fields. The bridge writes these into per-image `.mdf` files via `FrameMedia.UpdateMediaDefinition` (FrameMedia.java:912). The bridge's orient-lock filter (`MediaList.checkMediaValid` calling `media.getRatio()`) reads the .mdf width/height to decide whether each playlist item matches the frame's orientation.

**Therefore: aa.width/aa.height MUST be SOURCE image dims for bridge clients, regardless of what the MP4 container's dims are.** The MP4 video pipeline (VP) encodes to frame.Width × frame.Height for Meural bridges, but that's irrelevant to the .mdf metadata — the bridge never reads MP4 container dims for filtering decisions.

The previous code (pre-3361172d, comment claimed "mdf must reflect what was actually shipped") returned frame target dims for Meural bridges, which made every cached item appear to have the frame's exact ratio. The orient-lock filter `Math.abs(frame_ratio - media_ratio) < 0.5` always evaluated true → every image passed → mixed-orientation playlists rotated indiscriminately on portrait/landscape bridges.

**Customer impact:** fleet-wide latent; only manifests on bridges with mixed-orientation playlists + orient-lock flag bit set (Frame.Flags & 8). Single-orientation playlists hid it.

Pi/legacy frames have a different aa dims path (layout-derived with optional scale-to-fit). They MAY have the same latent bug — the layout dims also aren't source dims after crop — but no symptom reports. If the same orient-lock filter runs on Pi-side, that's a follow-up to investigate.

Reference: backlog_3fa8f166bc88-adjacent (frames-team's bug filing TBD), commit 3361172d, msg_904878d8a2af (frames-team diagnosis), msg_81db873d602a (server reply).

docs.title: Pre-27.16 cached .jpg-named-MP4 files persist on bridges that didn't get explicit clearMediaCache
docs.content:
# Pre-27.16 cached .jpg-named-MP4 files persist on bridges that didn't get explicit clearMediaCache

After the picFrame 27.16 MediaGetter ext-detection fix (commit 20c36c6, backlog_e12bc716d7a7), bridges correctly write MP4 bytes to .mp4 files for new fetches of Meural+JPG cohort items. BUT: bridges that already had pre-fix `.jpg`-named-MP4 files in cache do NOT auto-purge them. The fix only triggers on NEW downloads via MediaGetter.requestMedia. Existing on-disk wrong-named files persist.

Verified 2026-05-10 on .47 + .70 bench bridges: each has ~18 .jpg files in art/0 and art/1 whose magic bytes are `ISO Media, MP4 Base Media v1` — leftovers from pre-27.16. Sizes match real JPG sizes coincidentally because that's what the wrong cache happened to be.

Symptom if these get pushed: MeuralDisplay.getMimeType returns image/jpeg by extension, Meural responds {status:pass} but never displays (learning_794 silent-fail).

Mitigation paths in priority order:
1. **Field bridges with reported display issues**: send `clearMediaCache` MQTT command targeting the affected mediaIds → forces re-fetch → fixed by 27.16 path. Already done for rreed (588) + Doug (589) when server-team fix landed.
2. **Field bridges silently affected**: no proactive sweep yet. Would need a one-shot tool to walk all v27 bridges and wipe pre-27.16 cache files. Lower urgency since the only impact is the specific stale mediaIds, and they only matter if they're still in active playlists.
3. **Bench bridges**: leave alone during soak windows; clean as one-off when not actively soaking.

Diagnostic recipe (per bridge):
```bash
ssh root@<bridge-ip>
# count buggy files (jpg-named-MP4):
for f in /usr/local/bin/meurals/*/art/*/*.jpg; do
  head -c 12 "$f" | od -c | head -1 | grep -q ftyp && echo "BUGGY: $f"
done
# OR via file:
find /usr/local/bin/meurals/*/art -name '*.jpg' | xargs -I{} sh -c 'file -b "$1" | grep -q "ISO Media" && echo BUGGY: $1' _ {}
```

NOT auto-purging during 1.15.10 Alpha soak — would introduce re-download variables into the soak signal. Defer cleanup decision until soak completes + Init/Normal promoted.

docs.title: Bridge admin commands route via BridgeCommandRouter (string command field), NOT Commands_E enum / per-frame topic
docs.content:
# Bridge admin commands route via BridgeCommandRouter (string command field), NOT Commands_E enum / per-frame topic

When wiring an admin bridge button to the nimbus-agent, the right path is:

- **Server side**: `BridgeCommandRouter.Instance.SendBridgeCommand(bridgeUuid, jsonString)` which publishes to topic `bridge/<bridgeUuid>/commands` (file: `picFrameServiceLibrary/BridgeCommandRouter.cs:100-114`). Payload is a flat JSON object `{command:"<name>", requestId, ...optionalFields}` — NOT a `JSONCommand` / `Commands_E` envelope.
- **Agent side**: dispatcher at `nimbus-agent/internal/meural/commands.go:93-128` switches on the `command` field. As of 1.15.7+, accepted commands are: `scanMeurals`, `pairMeural`, `unpairMeural`, `probeMeural`, `restartAgent`, `restartBridge` (full OS reboot), `restartMeural` (with optional `frameUuid`), `otaCheckNow`. Anything else returns `UNKNOWN_COMMAND`.

**Stale buttons discovered (separate bug):** `adminEditBridge.aspx` had `sendCommand('restart')` and `sendCommand('update')` buttons. The agent does NOT recognize `restart` or `update` — they fall through to UNKNOWN_COMMAND. Fixed `restart` → `restartAgent` as part of `backlog_5160a9dedfc2`. `update` should become `otaCheckNow` and `status` has no agent equivalent (consider removing the button or implementing a status command). Filed as a follow-up.

**Backlog description was stale on the route**: `backlog_5160a9dedfc2` mentioned `Frame.SendFrameCommandAsync(Commands_E.restartAgent|restartMeural, ...)` and `NimbusCommon/JSONCommand.cs` enum changes. That is the wrong path — those are for the legacy `frame/<uuid>/commands` topic which the bridge agent does NOT listen on. The bridge agent only listens on `bridge/<uuid>/commands`. No `Commands_E` enum changes are needed for any bridge command added post-1.15.6.

**Per-Meural dispatch quirk**: `restartMeural` with no `frameUuid` restarts ALL Meurals on the bridge via `supervisor.RestartAll()`. With `frameUuid`, restarts only that JVM via `StopMeural`+`StartMeural` (commands.go:173-220). Useful for both bulk and surgical recovery.

docs.title: picFrameClient :36010 IPC has multi-second cold-boot window — looks like crash to bleServer
docs.content:
# picFrameClient :36010 IPC has multi-second cold-boot window — looks like crash to bleServer

picFrameClient's `:36010` ControlServer IPC listener is bound from `ControlServer.run()` invoked at PicFrameClient.java:245 — INSIDE the run() method, which only fires after the synchronous `PicFrameClient(server)` constructor completes (lines 80-129).

The constructor does heavy synchronous work before scheduling run():
- L82 `mHW = CreateHWInterface()` — Pi GPIO + Hardware()
- L96 `ConfigData.loadConfig()`
- L100 `mHW.getPanelPower()`, L103 `mHW.CheckVideoOutput()` — hardware probes (can hang on KMS/DRM)
- L109 `new MediaGetter()`, L110 `new MediaManager()` — MediaManager loads serialized playlists (large for big collections)
- L114 `new SSDP()` — async thread spawned
- L115 `start(60000, ...)` — schedules run() thread

Window from JVM start until `:36010` is bound: typically 5-30s on a healthy frame, multi-minute on a degraded frame (slow disk, large playlist, hardware probe stalls).

bleServer is started independently (systemd / launcher) and is ready well before picFrame's IPC. So a BLE WiFi-rescue arriving during picFrame's cold boot gets `dial tcp [::1]:36010 → connection refused`. To bleServer/mobile this is **indistinguishable from picFrame having crashed** — same connection refused, same silent failure. JVM is alive and healthy; the IPC port simply doesn't exist yet.

This caused the test19/frame 609 incident on 2026-05-10 11:17 (mobile-team msg_6f448dd245de). Earlier 10:59 attempt worked because picFrame was in steady state.

SSDP NPE in the same incident is a red herring — caught by SSDP.java:128 general Exception handler, sleeps 10s, retries. Doesn't kill JVM, doesn't affect ControlServer.

For diagnosis: when bleServer logs `connection refused` on :36010, do NOT assume picFrame is dead. JVM uptime + recent log activity proves nothing about IPC readiness — only an explicit `lsof -i :36010` or `ss -tlnp '( sport = :36010 )'` confirms the listener is up.

docs.title: Legacy frame fleet (26.19 and earlier) is fully immutable — no OTA possible during rescue
docs.content:
# Legacy frame fleet (26.19 and earlier) is fully immutable — no OTA possible during rescue

Constraint clarified by Tom 2026-05-10 during BLE rescue analysis: legacy frames running 26.19 or earlier are entirely immutable. We cannot ship updates of any kind to them — including bleServer, picFrameClient, log4j configs, or sidecars.

Catch-22 specifically for the BLE rescue path: any fix to bleServer (e.g. write `wpa_supplicant.conf` directly, decouple from picFrame :36010) would require an OTA, but OTAs require network, which is exactly what's broken when rescue is needed. The fix can't reach the frames that need it.

Implication for any "rescue-class" failure on legacy frames: the only available knobs are external to our code — power-cycle workaround, mobile UX copy, support documentation. No frame-side fix is possible. Don't propose one.

Future-fleet (v27+ on `mqtt` branch) IS fixable. Hardening goes there. Legacy gets failure-mode documentation only.

Trap to avoid: when investigating a legacy-frame issue, the natural instinct is to think "the fix is in bleServer / picFrameClient." That's correct for v27+ but useless for legacy. Always check version posture before proposing remediation.

docs.title: FrameRescue on legacy 26.19 frames is bounded by picFrame.jar IPC cold-boot window
docs.content:
# FrameRescue on legacy 26.19 frames is bounded by picFrame.jar IPC cold-boot window

picFrame.jar's :36010 IPC listener (used by bleServer to dispatch BLE WiFi commits) binds inside `run()` AFTER a synchronous constructor that includes hardware probes + panel-power detection + video-output check + MediaManager init (deserializing playlists from disk). On cold boot this takes 30s-3min before :36010 is reachable.

During that window, bleServer accepts BLE writes (CharApSelect/PskCount/Psk0..N/PskCommit) but `dial tcp [::1]:36010` returns "connection refused", so the WiFi push is silently discarded. wpa_supplicant.conf is never updated, frame never associates, mobile's verify polls AP="" for the full 60s budget and times out.

Confirmed by frames-team (nimbus msg_98db4dc2d31a, 2026-05-10) after walking picFrameClient source. Same code path as a working rescue; the only difference is picFrame's uptime (steady-state vs cold-booting). 10:45 UTC bench succeeded because picFrame had been up since 09:17 UTC. 11:32 UTC bench failed because picFrame had restarted at 11:17 UTC and was still in its cold-boot window.

**No mobile fix possible for 26.19**: legacy frames are immutable, can't ship bleServer or picFrame updates. The v27+ "bleServer becomes authoritative for wpa_supplicant.conf writes + falls back to picFrame IPC for state notification" fix is in frames-team's queue but only helps the post-mqtt-branch fleet.

**Mobile mitigation (commit 50005ee)**: VerifyStep.ShowFailureUI rewritten to call out the cold-boot scenario — tells the user to wait ~2 min and retry, or power-cycle and wait if it's been on for a while. Captive-portal mention preserved as a tail (frame-associated-no-internet path actually hits the happy-path with Inet=False, not this failure UI).

**Diagnosing in the field**: if bleServer.log shows `dial tcp [::1]:36010: connection refused` around the time of the BLE WiFi push, that's the cold-boot or crashed-picFrame failure. Power-cycle + wait fixes the cold-boot variant; crashed-picFrame requires intervention.

docs.title: BleBluetoothService discovery cache must NOT be cleared on every scan
docs.content:
# BleBluetoothService discovery cache must NOT be cleared on every scan

`BleBluetoothService.ScanForNimbusAsync` previously called `_discoveredDevices.Clear()` at the start of every scan. That broke the FrameRescue handoff: TroubleshootPage's diagnose scan populated the cache, user tapped "Configure WiFi", FrameSetupPage's constructor unconditionally called `ShowStep(SetupStep.Scan)` which fired ScanStep.OnStepShown → ScanForNimbusAsync → cache cleared. Then ApplyQueryAttributes transitioned to WifiStep, whose ConnectAndLoadAsync called ConnectToDeviceAsync(guid) — guid wasn't in the now-empty cache → "Frame not found" exception → rescue dies.

Removed the Clear() in commit 206519d. The dict's only consumers are ConnectToDeviceAsync (line 204) and DisconnectAsync (line 493) lookups by Guid. ScanStep's UI uses the local `devices` list returned from each scan, NOT the dict — so accumulating entries across scans is harmless. TryAdd already dedupes by Id. Stale entries from a long-since-vanished frame just produce a "connection failed" timeout if the user tries to connect to one, which is debuggable.

**Don't re-add the Clear()** — it'll break FrameRescue. If stale-entry accumulation ever becomes a memory or UX problem, prune by IDevice.State==Disconnected mtime instead.

docs.title: MAUI Shell navigation: registered routes use relative paths; round-trip uses `..?`
docs.content:
# MAUI Shell navigation: registered routes use relative paths; round-trip uses `..?`

Pages registered via `Routing.RegisterRoute(nameof(FrameSetupPage), typeof(FrameSetupPage))` MUST be navigated to with relative paths (`Shell.Current.GoToAsync($"{nameof(FrameSetupPage)}?...")`). The `//FrameSetupPage` absolute-route form is reserved for ShellContent items in the Shell hierarchy — using it on a registered route throws a navigation exception that crashes whatever called it.

The TroubleshootPage→FrameSetupPage rescue handoff initially used `//FrameSetupPage?mode=FrameRescue&...` — crashed the moment user tapped "Configure WiFi". Fixed in beb3e1f.

For round-trip back to a page that's already in the stack (e.g. FrameSetupPage's FrameRescue → TroubleshootPage with continueAfterWifi=true): use `Shell.Current.GoToAsync("..?key=value&...")` to pop with query attributes. Pushing a fresh instance via `nameof(TroubleshootPage)?...` would leave a stale TroubleshootPage below it on the stack.

[QueryProperty] setters fire on both push and pop in Shell — pop+query delivers attributes to the existing page just like a fresh push would.

docs.title: VerifyStep: 0.0.0.0 is not a valid IP; char-mode needs longer poll budget
docs.content:
# VerifyStep: 0.0.0.0 is not a valid IP; char-mode needs longer poll budget

Two coupled fixes in VerifyStep for the WiFi-rescue verify loop:

**Don't accept "0.0.0.0" as a valid IpAddress** (commit 193c33c). When wpa_supplicant associates fast but DHCP hasn't completed, the frame reports `AP=<ssid>` and `IpAddress="0.0.0.0"`. The original check used `!string.IsNullOrEmpty(IpAddress)` which accepted that — set Context.DeviceIp="0.0.0.0", fired SSH probe at 0.0.0.0 (always reachable=False), and auto-advanced to round-trip. TroubleshootPage's continueAfterWifi handler then ran `RunRepairAsync("0.0.0.0", skipConfirm:true)` against a bogus address. Now explicitly excluded; loop keeps polling until DHCP lands a real IP.

**Char-mode needs 20 attempts (60s) vs UART's 8 (24s)** (commit 0bd9a70). Pre-UART (≤26.20) frames take 30-60s for `wpa_cli reconfigure` + DHCP after a credential push. The original 8-attempt budget timed out in ~24s, landing users on the failure UI even when the frame was about to come online. UART/agent path responds faster; doesn't need the headroom.

`int maxAttempts = autoPlay ? 3 : (_ble.IsCharacteristicMode ? 20 : 8);`

`WifiStep.ConfigureAccountWifiAsync` originally used `acct.Passcode ?? ""`. If the server's `api/Mobile/getWifiList` returned no passcode for an SSID (legacy entries, open networks, deletion), we silently shipped an empty PSK to the frame — wpa_supplicant correctly rejected it on a secured network → frame never associated → mobile's verify timed out indefinitely with no diagnostic.

The empty-PSK guard added in commit 30ac221 only covered the scanned-network path; account-WiFi auto-connect bypassed it.

docs.content:
# abydos Serilog→Loki path resolves via LokiUrl AppSetting hand-added to live Web.config (not in repo)

2026-05-10: While answering server-team's Loki Q1, verified the Serilog→Loki path on abydos is live (latest stream entry within minutes of the check). Mechanism:

1. SerilogConfig.cs resolution order: env var NIMBUS_LOKI_URL → AppSetting LokiUrl → fallback http://10.7.0.1:3100 (Azure, dead).
2. No IIS app pool on abydos has any environment variables set. Checked all 5 pools (.NET v4.5, .NET v4.5 Classic, DefaultAppPool, NimbusProd, NimbusStaging) — all empty.
3. The URL is resolved via AppSetting fallback: C:\inetpub\nimbus-staging\Web.config:191 has `<add key="LokiUrl" value="http://10.100.0.1:3100" />`.
4. The repo's picFrameWeb/Web.config does NOT contain this key. It was hand-added on the live Web.config post-cutover and persists because deploy.sh excludes Web.config from the publish step.

**Fragility:** Any Web.config replacement on abydos that drops the LokiUrl key would silently break the path. SerilogConfig.cs:102-106 wraps GrafanaLoki sink configuration in try/catch; connection failures are swallowed with only a Debug.WriteLine — the path can be dead and the app would not surface an error.

**Robustness options to consider:**
- Bake LokiUrl into a Web.config.Release transform so it's deployed deterministically.
- OR set NIMBUS_LOKI_URL on the IIS app pool environment variables (Set-WebConfiguration on system.applicationHost/applicationPools/add[@name='NimbusStaging']/environmentVariables). Belt-and-suspenders.
- Pair with a Loki-side liveness alert: Grafana alert if `count_over_time({service="web-server"}[1h]) == 0` to catch a silently dead path.

**Stream labels currently emitted by abydos:** app=nimbus, environment=staging, host=NIMBUSWEB, service=web-server. host=NIMBUSWEB is abydos's Windows hostname (verified `hostname` = NimbusWeb). Not canonical per interface:layer1-loki-backend v1.0.0 — migration to canonical host/service/level/frame_id schema is a separate server-team task.

docs.title: ASMX page methods do NOT respect C# default parameter values — JSON body must include every parameter
docs.content:
# ASMX page methods do NOT respect C# default parameter values — JSON body must include every parameter

# ASMX/page-method JSON binding: optional C# parameters are runtime-required

When a `[WebMethod]` static page method on an .aspx is called from JS via
`fetch('/Page.aspx/Method', {method:'POST', body: JSON.stringify({...})})`,
the request enters ASP.NET's `JsonDataContractDeserializer` (the
ScriptMethod machinery). That deserializer matches JSON properties to C#
parameter names by name. **It does not honor C# default values.**

A method declared `public static string Foo(int a, string b, string c = null)`
called with body `{"a":1,"b":"x"}` will throw before the method body runs:

> Invalid web service call, missing value for parameter: 'c'.

ASP.NET returns HTTP 500 with `{"Message":"...","ExceptionType":"...","StackTrace":"..."}`
— **not** wrapped in the `{"d": ...}` envelope. JS code doing
`fetch().then(r=>r.json()).then(d => d.d)` sees `d.d === undefined`.

## Symptom

Page button silently prints `< undefined` (or whatever your no-d-property
fallback renders). No log entry from the WebMethod body. IIS log shows the
POST returning 500.

## Wrong fix

Don't think the issue is the JSON envelope or the fetch wrapping — it
isn't. The error envelope is the *consequence* of binding failure, not the
cause.

## Right fix

Always include every parameter in the JS body, using `null` for unused:

```js
var body = { hwId: hwId, command: command, frameUuid: frameUuid || null };
```

The C# side typically already handles null via `string.IsNullOrEmpty(...)`,
so no server change is needed.

## When this bites you

- Adding a new optional parameter to an existing WebMethod called from
  multiple JS sites — every existing call site silently breaks.
- Migrating from a 2-arg WebMethod to a 3-arg one without updating callers.
- Page methods are the worst offender; full WCF / Web API don't behave this
  way.

## Verified instance

2026-05-10: extended `Admin/adminEditBridge.aspx.cs::SendBridgeCommand`
from `(hwId, command)` to `(hwId, command, frameUuid = null)` for the
per-Meural Restart button. Existing buttons (Scan Meurals, Status, Restart
Bridge, Update) all silently broke — page printed `< undefined`. Fix was
one-line JS: always include frameUuid in body. Committed in two commits
back-to-back; the original signature change should have included the JS
update in the same commit.

# picFrameClient builds standalone, NOT via reactor -pl

Build picFrameClient from its OWN directory:

  cd Frames/raspframe/picFrameClient
  mvn clean package -DskipTests

NOT via reactor from `Frames/raspframe` with `-pl picFrameClient -am` — that errors with "Could not find the selected project in the reactor: picFrameClient". Version is in `picFrameClient/pom.xml` line 7 `<version>X.YY</version>`. Bumping pom.xml regenerates `picFrameClient/dependency-reduced-pom.xml` which also has the version — both get committed together (the dependency-reduced-pom is checked in despite being maven-shade-plugin-generated).

Java 8 compat is mandatory for picFrameClient. Build doesn't enforce it (compiler/release source/target settings are in pom but verify before merging anything questionable). Stick to JDK 1.0–1.8 APIs only.

The maven-shade build emits a wall of overlapping-resource WARNINGs (META-INF/LICENSE etc. across pi4j-*, httpclient/httpcore, jackson-*, log4j, etc.). Those are pre-existing and not signal — only fail on actual ERROR or BUILD FAILURE.

docs.content:
# Comm-type discriminator for rescue-attempt logging is _ble.IsCharacteristicMode

The rescue-attempt v1 spec's `comm` field has values preuart|uart|unknown. Mapping: `_ble.IsCharacteristicMode == true` → preuart (fw ≤26.20, characteristic-only API). `false` → uart (covers BOTH legacy UART fw 26.21-27.01 AND nimbus-agent v27.02+; v1 spec doesn't distinguish those). The discriminator is only valid AFTER ConnectToDeviceAsync because SetupCharacteristicsAsync sets the flag during service-tree resolution. So SetComm must be called post-connect: WifiStep.ConnectAndLoadAsync (line 71-73) and FrameDiagnosticService.DiagnoseAsync (line 59-61). Phase 2 (FrameRepairService.RepairFrameAsync) has NO BLE access — it cannot determine comm-type and inherits whatever earlier-phase code set on the active attempt. Don't try to infer comm in Phase 2 from manifest version; the BLE-phase signal is authoritative.

docs.title: Grafana 12.4 alert-rules YAML provisioning: key is `execErrState`, not `executionErrorState`
docs.content:
# Grafana 12.4 alert-rules YAML provisioning: key is `execErrState`, not `executionErrorState`

In Grafana 12.4 (`/usr/share/grafana/bin/grafana server -v` = 12.4.2), the alert-rule provisioning YAML key for query-error behavior is **`execErrState`** (camelCase, short form), NOT `executionErrorState`. The latter is silently ignored — Grafana reads the file without error, applies sibling fields (expr, for, labels, annotations, data), but the rule's execErrState retains its existing DB value.

**Confusing source:** `/etc/grafana/provisioning/alerting/sample.yaml` shipped with Grafana 12.4 still references `executionErrorState`. That sample is stale on this key.

**Valid values for execErrState:** `OK`, `Alerting`, `Error`. (Same set as the API field of the same name.)

**Why this matters:** if you only do a `curl POST /api/admin/provisioning/alerting/reload` or `systemctl restart grafana-server` and verify by glancing at the file diff, you'll think the change took effect. The query body updates (because `expr` is under the `data[].model` block and uses correct key names) — but the top-level `execErrState` will silently retain its old value. Always verify via API: `curl /api/v1/provisioning/alert-rules/<uid> | jq .execErrState`.

**Fix pattern:** mass-rename in YAML, scp, install (preserve grafana group ownership at 644), then `systemctl restart grafana-server` (reload endpoint also works for fresh load but takes >5s of effective downtime; the restart is comparable). Verify all rules' execErrState via /api/v1/provisioning/alert-rules/{uid}.

Encountered while fixing `backlog_60043ba5ad90` (Grafana false-fire on Loki 500-series cap). Final state in `infra/stargate/grafana/nimbus-alert-rules.yaml` uses `execErrState` everywhere.

docs.title: Loki LogQL: `| json | count_over_time(...)` without `sum()` hits 500-series cap on busy streams
docs.content:
# Loki LogQL: `| json | count_over_time(...)` without `sum()` hits 500-series cap on busy streams

When you write a LogQL query like `count_over_time({app="nimbus"} | json | level="error" [15m])`, Loki extracts every distinct JSON-label combination from matching log lines into its own series, then runs count_over_time per series. On a moderately busy stream (Nimbus's web-server logs at ~4-15 errors per 15-30m window) this exceeds Loki's default 500-series-per-query cap. The query returns an error like `maximum of series (500) reached for a single query`.

**Symptoms:**
- Grafana alert annotation reads `sse.dataQueryError ... maximum of series (500) reached`
- `errors=-1 threshold=-1` (sentinel values for query failure) in the alert payload
- If the rule has `execErrState: Alerting`, the alert false-fires on the query error, not real data

**Fix:** wrap in `sum()` so all per-label series collapse into a single scalar before count_over_time evaluates:

```
sum(count_over_time({app="nimbus"} | json | level="error" [15m]))
```

If you want per-label-aggregated breakdowns, do them in panels (where the 500 cap is more permissive), not in alert queries. Alert queries should always reduce to scalars before the threshold expression.

**Defense:** always pair this with `execErrState: OK` on the alert rule (Grafana 12.4 YAML key — NOT `executionErrorState`, see learning_412) so any future query-error mode doesn't false-fire.

**Where this matters in Nimbus:** any Grafana alert that queries `{app="nimbus" or "web-server"} | json | ...` from Loki on stargate. Initial fix landed for all 5 nimbus-error-* rules in `infra/stargate/grafana/nimbus-alert-rules.yaml` (2026-05-10, backlog_60043ba5ad90).

docs.title: nimbus-agent loses /commands SUBSCRIBE on every Paho reconnect (CleanSession + missing handler)
docs.content:
# nimbus-agent loses /commands SUBSCRIBE on every Paho reconnect (CleanSession + missing handler)

**Structural bug in nimbus-agent ≤1.15.10. Fixed in 1.15.11 (frames-team commit pending, OTA via Alpha cg 19).**

## Mechanism (frames-team root-cause, msg_0cc35cefa437)

Two SUBSCRIBE paths exist; only one is wired to reconnect:

1. `internal/mqtt/cloud.go:120-133` — `OnConnectHandler` calls `cc.subscribeConfig(c)` and stops. Only `/config` is re-subscribed on every connect/reconnect.
2. `internal/meural/commands.go:62-67` — `BridgeHandler.Start()` subscribes to `bridge/<uuid>/commands` **once at process startup**, called from `startBridgeCloud` in `cmd/nimbus-agent/main.go:208`. `startBridgeCloud` is a once-pattern (early-returns if `cloudClient != nil`).

`CleanSession=true` (`cloud.go:114`) + `AutoReconnect=true` (`cloud.go:109`): Paho reconnects automatically but does NOT auto-resubscribe — broker wipes prior subs on every CleanStart=1 CONNACK, so the client MUST re-issue every SUBSCRIBE in the OnConnect handler. Only `/config` lives there. Every reconnect = `/commands` permanently dropped until the agent process restarts.

## Symptoms

- All admin commands (Scan/Status/Restart/Update/per-Meural ops) silently disappear at the broker on a bridge that has reconnected at least once since its last process restart.
- Web side sees clean publish + ACK. Bridge journal shows no `BridgeCmd: received` line. No error anywhere.
- A fresh process start (systemd watchdog, deploy, manual `systemctl restart nimbus-agent`) restores `/commands` until the next reconnect.

## Earlier wrong framing (superseded)

I previously titled this a "SUBSCRIBE race" — that was wrong. There is no timing window; there is no `/commands` resubscribe code on the reconnect path at all. The drop is deterministic, not racy.

## Recovery for in-the-wild broken bridges

- Republishing retained `/config` does NOT trigger a re-handshake (Paho dispatches to existing handler, no disconnect).
- Mosquitto has no broker-side kick without dynamic-security plugin (not loaded on stargate).
- Only in-place fix: SSH + `systemctl restart nimbus-agent` per bridge.
- Fleet-level fix: 1.15.11 OTA carries forward via normal poll timer.

## Detection (until 1.15.11 lands everywhere)

From stargate mosquitto.log: for each `bridge_<uuid>_agent` clientid currently CONNECT'd, check whether the post-CONNACK SUBSCRIBE chain includes `/commands`. Missing = broken. Frames-team has a script for this.

## Spec context

Restart Bridge backlog `5160a9dedfc2` was blocked on this. Server-side code (commits `67b3b747`, `0aa087e4`) is correct and deployed; bridges with subscribed `/commands` accept the command and act on it. Bridges in the broken-subscribe state will silently drop the publish until 1.15.11 lands.

## Related UX gotcha (separate item)

`restartAgent` (and `restartBridge`) kill the process before `CommandResponse` can be published. Success signal is the bridge going offline ~5s then `status/online=true` retained republish — not a JSON return. Admin buttons waiting for JSON will time out. Filed as separate backlog item for UX toast.

docs.title: Frame-autofix v1 bench test 2026-05-11: 5 mobile bugs + test19 JKS death root cause
docs.content:
# Frame-autofix v1 bench test 2026-05-11: 5 mobile bugs + test19 JKS death root cause

Bench-tested Frame-autofix v1 (eb79596) on iPhone XR / test19 (SW 26.19, pre-UART) on 2026-05-11. Cold-boot rescue scenario FAILED. SD-card forensics on nimbus-pi (.77) per learning_0342e9c4232d4b5b uncovered five distinct mobile bugs + a frame-side root cause.

## Bench result

Tom tapped Configure WiFi → wizard pushed `LemmonsLakeHouse` creds via BLE → bleServer.log proves the BLE protocol worked perfectly (received SSID, 2 passkey segments correctly concatenated to "Household of the Lemmons", final flag, dispatched to picFrame IPC, waited 20s, no response, returned `status is failure`). Mobile DID NOT detect the failure and advanced to VerifyStep, where ~12 minutes of polling exhausted and ShowFailureUI rendered. Zero `rescue_attempt` rows logged to `nimbus.AppEvents` (Tom's UserId=12, 30-min window).

## Mobile bugs (in severity order)

**#4 [CRITICAL] CharacteristicWifiSetupAsync always returns true.**
`NimbusMaui/Services/BleBluetoothService.cs:1234-1265` — writes SSID + PSK segments + commit char then `return true` unconditionally. No read-back, no status char check. Pre-UART frames (≤26.18) have no BLE feedback characteristic for setupWifi by design, so mobile is blind to bleServer's "status is failure". The success path advances to VerifyStep, then ~12 min of doomed polling.

**#5 [HIGH] VerifyStep ShowFailureUI does not call RescueAttempts.End().**
`NimbusMaui/Pages/SetupSteps/VerifyStep.xaml.cs:292` — adds `ServerUnreachable` problem then waits for Retry/Back/ContinueAnyway button. If user just stares at the screen (most common reaction), the rescue_attempt is never finalized → no telemetry. Breaks Tom's 2026-05-10 directive that EVERY offline frame logs an attempt.

**#1 [MEDIUM] VerifyStep ResetUI paints WiFi=✅ from context.WifiSsid.**
`VerifyStep.xaml.cs:36-40` — if context has a WifiSsid set (which WifiStep always sets in OnWifiConnected), VerifyStep shows the green checkmark immediately. Tom literally said "wifi was connected" because the icon was green BEFORE any verification ran. Misleading UX in exactly the failure case where we need it to be honest.

**#3 [LOW] 20 ble_connect events fired in 1 minute** for the same frame (test19, BLE name "Nimbus Frame #5b4d107b") during the bench attempt. Not retried wifi pushes — actual `ble_connect` AppEvent spam. Probably WifiStep's BLE retry-on-failure loop + periodic rescan each emitting the event. Find emit site, throttle to once per session.

**#6 [HIGH for QoR] Phase 2 "always-run" never reaches this scenario.**
The 2026-05-10 directive says every Troubleshoot run executes Phase 2 SSH-based recovery regardless of WiFi outcome. But Phase 2 requires SSH reachability, which requires WiFi, which requires picFrame Java running on the frame — exactly what's broken in this failure shape. Phase 2 can't run, so neither `jks_deploy` nor anything else fires. The autofix-must-run-end-to-end promise is unmet for the most common cold-boot symptom (dead Java).

## Frame-side root cause (test19, SW 26.19)

`/mnt/usb-data/logs/picFrame_2026-04-30T11:35:28.813Z.log` — last picFrame run **11 days ago**. Java died from:

```
SSLHandshakeException: PKIX path building failed: unable to find valid certification path
  at ServerConnector.serverConnect (ServerConnector.java:619)
```

NimbusFrame.jks (trust store) doesn't have a CA chain for the current server cert. Post-LE-cutover the JKS needs an updated root. picFrame's ShutdownTask fired after the SSL failure; new picFrame.log files would have been created on each subsequent launch attempt — they aren't there, so picFrame.jar isn't running at all (likely crash-loop fast enough that log4j never opens its file).

Frame-side wpa_supplicant.conf still says `ssid="nimbusframe"` / `psk="nimbusframe"` (the bench dev AP), mtime May 10 — yesterday's rescue attempt also failed to land because the dispatch chain bleServer→picFrame is broken.

bleServer alone is the only daemon running, hence: BLE connect works, BLE WiFi push is "received" but cannot reach picFrame's IPC, the actual wpa_supplicant.conf write never happens.

Frames-team scope: needs JKS refresh OR card rebuild. Tom is doing card rebuild on test19. Worth checking whether the customer fleet has the same JKS drift.

## How to apply
- Mobile-team: 5 backlog items filed for autofix v1.1 fixes (#4, #5, #1 ship together; #3 and #6 separately).
- Mobile-side defense for THIS scenario (Java-dead): when CharacteristicWifiSetupAsync's BLE writes "succeed" but VerifyStep's polling never sees a non-0.0.0.0 IP for ≥30s, surface a distinct error "frame software not responding — try rebooting it via BLE" rather than the generic "didn't come online" copy.
- Bench reproduction recipe: any pre-UART frame whose picFrame.jar isn't actually running will trigger #4. Faking it: kill picFrame manually, leave bleServer up, attempt wifi push from mobile, observe mobile cheerfully advance to VerifyStep.

docs.title: Learning from mobile-team
docs.content: Pre-UART BLE protocol has no feedback channel for wifi setup. Mobile-side CharacteristicWifiSetupAsync is structurally blind to bleServer's "status is failure" return — must infer outcome from post-commit characteristic polling. VerifyStep's ResetUI paints WiFi=✅ from context, fooling even the operator into reporting "wifi was connected" when no verification has occurred. ShowFailureUI without terminal RescueAttempts.End() makes failure scenarios invisible to telemetry. test19's specific death is JKS PKIX (post-LE-cutover trust drift) — Phase 2's jks_deploy can't reach it via SSH because circular trap.

docs.title: CleanSession=true + AutoReconnect=true requires manual resubscribe in OnConnectHandler
docs.content:
# CleanSession=true + AutoReconnect=true requires manual resubscribe in OnConnectHandler

Paho golang with `SetCleanSession(true) + SetAutoReconnect(true)`: the broker wipes broker-side subscription state on every CleanStart=1 CONNACK, but Paho does NOT auto-resubscribe — that's the user's job in OnConnectHandler. Any subscribe call OUTSIDE OnConnectHandler runs exactly once at the moment-of-call and is silently lost on the next reconnect.

This was the 1.15.10 /commands silent-drop bug: subscribeConfig was inside OnConnectHandler, but BridgeHandler.Start (subscribing /commands) ran once at process startup via a separate code path. After any Paho-driven reconnect, only /config was replayed. Symptom: admin-page commands (Restart, Scan, Pair, Probe, etc.) silently disappeared. No UNKNOWN_COMMAND. No error. Just void. Broker dropped the publish because no subscriber existed for that topic on the current connection.

Pattern to prevent: route ALL cross-reconnect subscriptions through CloudClient.RegisterTopic (nimbus-agent/internal/mqtt/cloud.go:236), which stores (topic, handler) pairs and replays them in OnConnectHandler after every CONNACK. The old CloudClient.Subscribe() method was removed in 1.15.11 to prevent re-introduction.

Diagnostic signature in mosquitto.log for this bug: after a "New client connected ... as bridge_*_agent" line, count the post-CONNACK SUBSCRIBE lines for that client. If only /config appears and not /commands, the agent is in the broken state. Recovery requires process restart (systemctl restart nimbus-agent) — re-publishing retained /config does NOT trigger resubscribe (Paho dispatches to existing handler; no disconnect).

Fix log line for forward verification: "CloudMQTT: resubscribing N registered topic(s) after CONNACK" appears in journalctl on every reconnect post-1.15.11.

docs.title: Trixie Pi has nft only — iptables binary is gone
docs.content:
# Trixie Pi has nft only — iptables binary is gone

On Raspbian Trixie (Pi Zero 2 W and Pi 4), /usr/sbin/iptables and /sbin/iptables do NOT exist. Only nftables: /usr/sbin/nft is the binary. Scripts using `iptables` will fail with "No such file or directory" — silent failure if running via SSH-bash where the error gets lost in pipeline.

Working nft pattern for "temporarily block outbound port X" (used to force Paho-driven MQTT reconnect on .47 for 1.15.11 fix verification):

  nft add table inet mqttblock
  nft 'add chain inet mqttblock output { type filter hook output priority 0; }'
  nft add rule inet mqttblock output tcp dport 8883 drop
  # ...wait...
  nft delete table inet mqttblock

Single-table cleanup (`nft delete table inet mqttblock`) tears down chain+rule atomically. Always pair the add with a `nohup` safety-net cleanup at T+N to guarantee removal even if foreground SSH dies. ss -K alone (with INET_DIAG_DESTROY) is NOT sufficient on Pi kernels — the established socket survives the kill attempt with the same local port.

docs.content:
# OTA self-heals broken-subscribe bridges — HTTP path independent of /commands

A nimbus-agent in the 1.15.10 /commands-broken state can still pull and apply OTA updates. The OTA path (ota.Updater.loop, nimbus-agent/internal/ota/updater.go:114) is a 1-hour timer firing HTTPS GET to /api/updates/index, completely independent of MQTT command dispatch. Even a bridge that is deaf to bridge/<uuid>/commands will still: (1) tick its OTA timer, (2) discover newer AgentVersion in its config-group, (3) HTTPS-download the binary, (4) atomic-replace + systemctl restart nimbus-agent. Process restart runs BridgeHandler.Start() fresh, which re-registers /commands via CloudClient.RegisterTopic (1.15.11+).

Implication for fleet rollout: bumping configgroups.AgentVersion to 1.15.11 self-heals broken bridges within ~1 hour of the bump (worst-case OTA poll interval). No manual SSH-restart needed. Latent customer-impact window during the rollout = max 1h of "admin commands may silently drop on any bridge that has reconnected pre-OTA" — but this is the same bug behavior we're fixing, not a new risk introduced by the rollout.

docs.title: Serilog Loki sink: `labels:` and `propertiesAsLabels:` must be disjoint for a given key
docs.content:
# Serilog Loki sink: `labels:` and `propertiesAsLabels:` must be disjoint for a given key

**The trap.** The Serilog.Sinks.Grafana.Loki configuration has two ways to set indexed Loki labels:
- `labels:` — a static `List<LokiLabel>` applied to every event with a constant value.
- `propertiesAsLabels:` — a `string[]` of property names; per-event property values become label values.

If the same key (e.g., `service`) appears in BOTH, the sink emits two labels with the same key, OR the second silently shadows the first. Either way, the per-event override you intended (via `.ForContext("service", "picframeclient")`) won't behave reliably. Loki queries can return weird results: streams split unexpectedly, or `{service="picframeclient"}` returns 0 results because the static label is taking precedence.

**The fix pattern.** To make a label overridable per event:
1. REMOVE the key from `labels:`
2. ADD the key to `propertiesAsLabels:`
3. Keep the default value via `.Enrich.WithProperty(key, defaultValue)` — that becomes the property value if no `.ForContext` override runs.

**Applied this session** in `SerilogConfig.cs` for `service` (moved) and `frame_id` (added new), so `MqttFrameLogHandler.ForwardToLoki` can push events tagged `service=picframeclient` with `frame_id=<uuid>` per the layer1-loki-backend v1.0 contract.

**Spec context.** `interface:layer1-loki-backend` v1.0 defines four indexed labels: `host`, `service`, `level`, `frame_id`. `host` and `frame_id` are inherently per-event; `service` is per-source but the source-mix in this AppDomain spans `web-server` (Serilog default) and `picframeclient` (MQTT-forwarded frame logs). Moving `service` to propertiesAsLabels covers both cases without splitting the logger config.

**How to verify after deploy.** Once Loki receives events, `curl -s 'http://10.100.0.1:3100/loki/api/v1/label/service/values'` should return both `web-server` (today's default) and `picframeclient` (from MqttFrameLogHandler) once frames-team flips rootLogger on .47. If only one shows up, propertiesAsLabels isn't applying — re-check the disjoint rule.

**Cross-references:** `interface:layer1-loki-backend` v1.0, `backlog_800557a75f7a` (this work), `backlog_d53cf0cf0a38` (canonical-label migration follow-up).

# test19 sdcard on .77: legacy 26.19 rig card with multiple concurrent picStartup boots

test19 SD card (4-partition build target on /dev/sdb when inserted via USB on .77 build host) is a **legacy Raspbian 8 jessie rig card** running an Apr-29 custom launchPic.sh that bypasses picFrameStart.jar and runs picFrame.jar (= 26.19, md5 42b1598b8f07e01fbf58cb8945b2043d, 331K, dated Apr 23 2021) directly via JDK 8 + JavaFX/eglfb.

Key findings from forensic syslog/log analysis without booting:

1. **picFrame.jar DOES run** — log4j initializes successfully (8x `log4j:WARN No such property [maxBackupIndex]` per Java instance is the normal init noise). Confirmed on May 10 boots at 09:17, 10:59, 11:17.

2. **THREE concurrent picStartup processes** at every reboot on May 10. picStartup.sh PIDs 403, 406, 409 all wrote "Starting noip" at 11:17:03 within same second. launch-26.19.log shows 3× "starting picFrame.jar (26.19) direct" entries per boot. Cause: SysVinit-style rc{2,3,4,5}.d/S02picStartup.sh symlinks present (Default-Start: 2 3 4 5). systemd-sysv-generator's LSB compat layer is activating picStartup.service multiple times across runlevel transitions. Result: 3 launchPic.sh + 3 bleServer + 3 Java instances race on framebuffer/sockets/files.

3. **systemd kills picStartup.service after 5 min** (LSB script wrapped as Type=oneshot; launchPic.sh's infinite while-loop never returns; default TimeoutStartSec=5min). But Java/bleServer children OFTEN survive (confirmed by 09:57 StackOverflowError logging 35 min after 09:22 systemd kill). Sometimes children are killed cgroup-style (no exit code logged then).

4. **picFrame.jar runtime failures observed**:
   - Apr 30 11:35: WatchDogTask reboot triggered by "PicFrameClient missed checkin"; SSL handshake fails with `PKIX path building failed` connecting to server (config.xml says `<Server address="frames" port="36004" protocol="26"/>` — old TCP port 36004 not on OVH; `frames` hostname has no /etc/hosts entry, only `frames.nimbusframe.net=51.81.243.11`); 26.19 NimbusFrame.jks (Mar 30 21315 bytes) does not trust current LE chain.
   - May 10 09:57: StackOverflowError in thread "ControlConnector" thrown from UncaughtExceptionHandler.
   - WiFi not configured on card; BLE WiFi setup attempted on May 10 11:21 (SSID LemmonsLakeHouse) FAILED at 11:22:15 ("command is bleWifiSetup status is failure"). Pi has never had a working network on May 10.

5. **Spurious May 1 NoClassDefFoundError org/apache/log4j/Logger** was a transient state (script files swapped between rig and `launchPic.sh.with-java.bak` production launcher) — not the current state. Current launchPic.sh on data partition explicitly puts `lib/log4j-1.2.17.jar` on -cp and lib/ exists with log4j-1.2.17.jar (Logger.class confirmed in archive). Current state log4j loads fine.

6. **Apparent "die immediately" symptom** is likely operator-side perception: with no WiFi → no server → SSL/PKIX cert errors → watchdog reboot loop → no on-screen frame content → display stays blank. Java processes ARE alive in the background but doing nothing useful. The triple-process race on later boots may cause faster death of all three from systemd cgroup kill OR resource conflict crashes.

Layout: /etc/init.d/picStartup.sh (case start: `/usr/local/bin/launchPic.sh`) → launchPic.sh forks bleServer subshell (& background) and runs `/opt/jdk1.8.0/bin/java ... -cp /lib4j/lib/*:./:lib/*:lib/log4j-1.2.17.jar:/opt/jdk1.8.0/jre/lib/jfxrt.jar:picFrame.jar net.nimbusframe.client.PicFrameApplication` in foreground while-loop with rc capture and `if rc=101 then reboot`. Init.manifest: `{"Id":8,"Name":"Init","Protocol":26,"Version":38,"LauncherVersion":21,"Server":"frames"}`. cmdline.txt: legacy (`dwc_otg.lpm_enable=0 console=ttyAMA0`). Kernel 4.4.45-v7+ #954 (2017). Machine: Pi 3 Model B Rev 1.2.

To diagnose live: SSH into the booted Pi (not .77 — .77 is just hosting the card via USB), tail /usr/local/bin/logs/launch-26.19.log, /usr/local/bin/logs/bleServer.log, and `tail -f /var/log/syslog | grep -E 'picStartup|java'`. Java stdout/stderr is captured to syslog with `picStartup.sh[PID]:` prefix.

docs.title: test19/26.19-rig card: picFrame.jar self-restarts because setupMode + rig launchPic both manage bleServer
docs.content:
# test19/26.19-rig card: picFrame.jar self-restarts because setupMode + rig launchPic both manage bleServer

Corrected analysis after Tom clarification (no internet → clock stuck; pre-v27 ran from launchPic.sh shell only, no systemd unit; test frame used for mobile-team rescue testing where BLE sends commands to picFrame.jar's local control socket).

**Where the rescue socket lives:** picFrame.jar's ControlServer listens on `[::1]:36010` (IPv6 localhost). bleServer.bin is the BLE→TCP bridge; it dials that port to deliver commands from the phone. Confirmed by bleServer.log lines like `Got error on connect:dial tcp [::1]:36010: connect: connection refused` repeated every second.

**Why the socket is dead (Apr 30 10:17 boot picFrame log):**

picFrame.jar starts and runs for **~9 seconds** then voluntarily restarts via `Raspberry.restartApp`. The cause chain:

1. `PicFrameClient.java:140` - "unique ID not found so doing hwInit" — this card has no Unique. `HWconfig.xml` is empty (`<Product id="0" name=""/>`); the wpa_supplicant only has LemmonsLakeHouse + nimbusframe entries with no network reachable.
2. `SetupMode changed to:notHWInit` → `setupThread` enters setup flow.
3. setupThread runs `wpa_cli wps_pbc` (WPS push-button pairing attempt).
4. `SetupMode changed to:wpsSetup`.
5. **CRITICAL CONFLICT**: setupThread runs `killall bleServer.bin; ./bleServer.bin` — picFrame.jar's setupMode owns the bleServer lifecycle and kills + respawns it. But the rig launchPic.sh ALSO runs bleServer in a background subshell with a 5-second restart loop. Two managers fighting over hci0 and bleServer pids.
6. New bleServer (picFrame's child) reports `State: PoweredOn` via stderr pipe at 10:17:15.
7. Concurrently ServerConnector hits `Network is unreachable` and resolves "NO gateway" at 10:17:16,394.
8. setupThread issues `new dialog:1` at PicFrameApplication.java:1055 (10:17:16,479).
9. ~160ms later JVM shutdown hook fires: `Recieved Shutdown hook` (PicFrameClient.java:98). Stack trace shows the hook is `PicFrameClient$1.run(line 99)` → `Raspberry.restartApp(line 324)`. Something inside that dialog-change path calls `System.exit` (most likely via `Platform.exit()` + JavaFX teardown, or directly).
10. Java exits. launchPic.sh's foreground while-loop respawns Java after `sleep 2`. Cycle repeats indefinitely.

**Why mobile rescue can't talk to the JAR:**
- ControlServer thread starts at PicFrameClient log 11.384 ("ControlServer.java:39 Thread Start:") — within first 4 sec
- JVM shuts down ~5 sec later (~10:17:16.6)
- So the listening socket on [::1]:36010 exists for only ~5 seconds out of every ~11-sec cycle. bleServer dials once per second, so it occasionally gets through but mostly hits "connection refused". The window is too narrow and chaotic for reliable command delivery.
- Additionally there are TWO bleServers fighting (rig launchPic.sh's + picFrame setupThread's). Either can be the one actually serving the phone's GATT, but only the one that survives the picFrame restart cycle would have a live FD to localhost:36010.

**Background death modes also seen (not the current symptom):**
- Apr 30 11:35 picFrame log: WatchDogTask reboot after 75 min ("PicFrameClient missed checkin last was 4548550"); side error `PKIX path building failed` connecting to staging.nimbusframe.net (26.19's NimbusFrame.jks doesn't trust current LE chain — but this is the SERVER socket, not the local rescue socket).
- May 10 09:57: `StackOverflowError thrown from the UncaughtExceptionHandler in thread "ControlConnector"` — local control server thread death (matters: that's exactly the rescue path; under some conditions the control thread itself crashes recursively).

**Fix-direction (NOT applied — Tom said research only):**
- The rig launchPic.sh should NOT run bleServer in a parallel subshell. The picFrame.jar's setupMode owns bleServer end-to-end (kills/respawns it on state transitions). Remove the `( while :; do … bleServer.bin … ) &` block from the rig launchPic.sh and let setupThread manage it.
- OR pre-provision a Unique ID + paymentDueDate + bright value + Product id on the test card so setupMode never triggers and the rescue socket stays up. (HWconfig.xml `Product id="0"` and config.xml `<Details Name=""/>` are giveaways.)
- The dialog:1 → System.exit transition itself is also questionable for a mobile-rescue test target — restarting on every dialog change destroys the rescue channel. Worth identifying what specifically sets dialog:1 (PicFrameApplication.java:1055) and whether it can be suppressed when in test/rescue mode.

Cmd to verify on a booted Pi (no changes): `ss -tlnp '( sport = :36010 )'` to see if anything is listening. `journalctl -t picStartup.sh -f` to watch Java stderr.

docs.title: Bridge phantom-Meural pattern: SQL DELETE of Frames row orphans the on-disk sandbox; reconcile never cleans it up
docs.content:
# Bridge phantom-Meural pattern: SQL DELETE of Frames row orphans the on-disk sandbox; reconcile never cleans it up

Reed's bridge 588 (`aaab08c4-86bf-4e0e-9590-c8630bce93fc`) running nimbus-agent 1.15.10. User reports Portrait Meural alternating between correct playlist and default placeholder.

**Diagnosis:** bridge `/status` reports 3 Meurals; server `/config` push lists only 2:
- `1450782e` (legit Portrait, Frame 608, MEU1118020008422, ip 192.168.68.99)
- `31fec42e` (legit Landscape, Frame 604, MEU1118020010033, ip 192.168.68.98)
- `9df16436-e22d-4b2a-95ee-20b7fceedd58` PHANTOM — same alias "miro-17", same ip 192.168.68.99 as legit Portrait. Not in server config push, not in picFrame.Frames, not in MqttAuth.

**Phantom origin** (picframe.frames_audit):
- Was Frame.Id=606 "Portrait" (uId=null, HWId=null — unclaimed/test row), MqttAuthId=598
- DELETE Action @ 2026-04-23 22:16:05 UTC by `root@localhost` (manual `DELETE FROM Frames` SQL session — NOT app code path)
- MqttAuth 598 also deleted (no row exists)
- LastConnection before deletion was 2026-04-19 14:56

**Why phantom keeps running:** nimbus-agent's `Supervisor.reconcileMeurals` (supervisor.go:850) loops `LoadMeuralConfigs()` against its in-memory `processes` map. It checks running-vs-configured-on-disk, never diffs against the server's retained `bridge/<uuid>/config` push. The on-disk sandbox `/usr/local/bin/meurals/9df16436-.../frame_config.json` has stayed because:
1. Reconcile only ADDS missing JVMs; never DELETES sandboxes orphaned by server-side row deletion.
2. The proper `unpairMeural` MQTT command (`commands.go:108 → handleUnpairMeural`) was never invoked — Tom deleted the row directly in SQL.

**What the phantom does:** on every agent start (and reconcile tick), a Java picFrame JVM is spawned for 9df16436:
- MQTT auth fails with `[AUTH FAIL] User: frame_9df16436-... - not found` in /var/log/mosquitto/auth.log (last attempt 2026-05-10 21:01:39 UTC; ~20 fails recorded since 2026-05-01).
- HTTP `POST /remote/postcard/` to 192.168.68.99 succeeds (Meural local API has no auth). The phantom posts default/empty playlist content, while the legit Portrait instance posts Reed's real playlist content. Both push at their own cadence → alternating display.

**Operational fix options (NOT applied — diagnostic only):**
- A. MQTT `unpairMeural` to bridge with the phantom frameUuid. Need to check whether `handleUnpairMeural` matches by IP or UUID — by IP risks tearing down the legit Portrait (shares 192.168.68.99). Safer if it takes UUID.
- B. SSH into bridge (CallHome reverse tunnel or LAN if Tom is on premises): `systemctl stop nimbus-agent; rm -rf /usr/local/bin/meurals/9df16436-e22d-4b2a-95ee-20b7fceedd58; systemctl start nimbus-agent`.
- C. Rename sandbox to `.9df16436-...` (dot-prefix sentinel that LoadMeuralConfigs already skips per supervisor.go:529, learning_b71). Reversible without deletion.

**Code fix (proper, longer-term):** bridge config-push handler should drive sandbox cleanup. On each `bridge/<uuid>/config` MQTT receipt, diff the server's `meurals[].uuid` list against `os.ReadDir(meurals/)`. Any UUID dir not in the server config and not dot-prefixed should be either auto-renamed to `.<uuid>` (safe) or removed (aggressive). Re-discovery would happen if the Meural re-pairs.

**Database-side prevention:** the root issue is that `DELETE FROM picFrame.Frames` doesn't propagate to bridges. Either (a) treat manual SQL delete as a forbidden operation for paired-Meural rows (use unpairMeural admin endpoint instead), or (b) make the BridgeController.PairMeural/UnpairMeural REST/MQTT path symmetric so server-side deletes always emit an unpair MQTT command before removing the row.

**Reproducer cost:** trivial. Repeat on any bridge: pair a Meural, then `DELETE FROM picFrame.Frames WHERE Id=X`. Bridge's on-disk sandbox lingers forever; phantom picFrame keeps posting to the Meural's IP until the bridge is reflashed or someone hand-cleans /usr/local/bin/meurals/.

docs.title: Hotspot rescue path validated end-to-end 2026-05-11: brick frame → online + displaying art
docs.content:
# Hotspot rescue path validated end-to-end 2026-05-11: brick frame → online + displaying art

Bench-tested the new HotspotRescuePage flow against test19 (SW 26.19, NimbusFrame.jks dead since 2026-04-30 from SSL PKIX failure). Result: **PASS end-to-end**. test19 went from `LastConnection: NULL` (never contacted server) to online, with picFrame.jar actively pulling playlist art (`MediaGetter`) and the iPhone app showing the frame as online displaying pictures. SW reported as 26.20 (was 26.19) — the picFrame.new launcher swap succeeded on reboot.

## What worked (vs the unknowns I'd flagged)
- **iOS MAUI's `NetworkInterface.GetAllNetworkInterfaces()` DOES see the hotspot/guest subnet.** Tom's router exposes the `nimbusframe` guest SSID as another AP on the same 192.168.15.0/24 as the main lemmons.net VLAN, so the scan range is /24 (~250 IPs) which `LanFrameSearchService` handles in ~5-15s.
- **CpuId discrimination works**: there were two Pis on the subnet (192.168.15.84 = test19, 192.168.15.199 = a different one). LanFrameSearchService SSH-probed both, matched test19's `5b4d107b` from `/proc/cpuinfo`, ignored the other.
- **Server-side first-contact provisioning self-heals**: Tom's hypothesis was correct. The frame had a missing manufacturing-first-connect unique-id file when this SD card was created. After fresh JKS + SSL handshake succeeded, server-side provisioning backfilled whatever state was missing — no special mobile-side handling needed.

## What surprised me / the central problem
**`NimbusApiClient.GetNimbusFileAsync` returned null on run #1 but succeeded on run #2.** Same code path, ~5 min apart, same logged-in user. JKS bytes were never returned the first time, so DeployJksAsync hit:
```
if (jksBytes == null || jksBytes.Length == 0) { result.AddError("Could not download NimbusFrame.jks from server"); return; }
```
The error was added to the result but `changesApplied = true` is set unconditionally right after DeployJks (line 180), so Reboot still fired and the frame rebooted with the stale Apr 30 JKS — useless reboot. Logged as `backlog_*` for v1.1 (see below). Likely root cause: an auth bearer state issue on the iPhone at that moment. Worth: (a) retry-on-failure inside DeployJks (re-fetch JKS once before AddError), (b) NOT setting `changesApplied = true` when JKS deploy failed (don't reboot with broken trust store; abort instead with a useful error).

## Mobile UI lies about progress during long stages
The Phase 2 rsync stages (RsyncLauncher / RsyncBundle / RsyncStartupTgz / DeployJks) emit ONE `RepairProgress` report each. Between reports the UI label sits unchanged for 30-90s on residential WAN, and `ProgressBar.Progress` is whatever was last set (35%, 55%, 65%). Tom hit cancel TWICE thinking the flow was hung. Each time the underlying flow was actually fine — eventually reached Reboot and frame state changed. Fix shipped in `f5566e8`: ActivityIndicator + ticking "Elapsed: Xs" timer + hint text on both HotspotRescuePage and TroubleshootPage.

## How to apply

docs.title: Defense-in-depth ACL pattern: guard ABOVE device_type dispatch
docs.content:
# Defense-in-depth ACL pattern: guard ABOVE device_type dispatch

For protecting a specific topic shape (e.g., bridge/+/cmd command channel), place the guard BEFORE the per-device_type dispatch in check_acl, not as an additional check inside each branch. Reason: existing branches include permissive cases (server: allowed=True; testuser: allowed=True; bridge: allowed for any topic under their own bridge/{hwid}/). A per-branch check requires editing every permissive branch and is brittle when new device_types are added. A top-of-function guard is one location, deny-by-default with explicit allow-list (only operator + server), and naturally extends as we add more sensitive topic shapes. Pattern: lookup device_type, then check sensitive-topic guards (each is `if topic_matches and op_matches: explicit allow/deny`), THEN fall through to the normal per-device_type dispatch. SUBSCRIBE and PUBLISH are differentiated via the acc parameter so guards can be acc-specific. Applied 2026-05-11 in auth_server.py for backlog_f51d17ba6d02.

docs.title: Wyze Cam Pan v3 (HL_PAN3) is incompatible with docker-wyze-bridge — protocol shift
docs.content:
# Wyze Cam Pan v3 (HL_PAN3) is incompatible with docker-wyze-bridge — protocol shift

2026-05-11: Tested docker-wyze-bridge v2.10.3 with a Wyze Cam Pan v3 (model HL_PAN3, firmware 4.50.16.6242) on both Windows Docker Desktop and Linux (sage, Docker 29.0.2, network_mode: host). Same failure pattern in both environments: HTTPS auth succeeds (auth, get_user_info, get_object_list all 200), camera is discovered, then `IOTC_Connect_ByUIDEx` times out after 20s with `[-13] IOTC_ER_TIMEOUT`. The camera is fully functional via the Wyze mobile app (live view works), but the bridge cannot reach it.

Root cause: Wyze has been progressively moving newer cameras (Pan v3 is one) off the legacy TUTK P2P protocol that docker-wyze-bridge uses, onto Wyze's own proprietary cloud protocol that only their official app speaks. Pan v3 advertises via the Wyze API (the bridge fetches it as model HL_PAN3) but doesn't register with TUTK cloud relay, so the bridge can't get a session token to talk to it.

This is NOT a config issue, NOT a NAT/networking issue, NOT a credentials issue. No amount of NET_MODE, DTLS, BOA_ENABLED, or host networking will resolve it.

How to apply: If a future watcher (or any future agent) is asked to use a Wyze Cam Pan v3 for an RTSP-style integration, refuse and recommend a different camera. Wyze Cam OG, Cam v3 (non-Pan), and older Cam v2 are still TUTK-supported as of 2026-05 per community reports — but the trend is bad. For new work, recommend RTSP-native cameras (Reolink, Amcrest) that don't depend on any Wyze-specific protocol.

Pan v3 is fine for general security monitoring via the Wyze app. Just not for our integration work.

# Eufy "RTSP to NAS" auto-disables after 2-3min and the listener only binds during active streaming

2026-05-11: Investigated Tom's existing Eufy HomeBase (at 192.168.15.118, MAC OUI 10:2c:b1 = Anker/Eufy) as a free alternative to buying new cameras. The Eufy app surfaces an RTSP URL like `rtsp://<user>:<pw>@<homebase-ip>:554/live6` and a toggle to enable RTSP for a given camera. Tested from sage after enabling the toggle and confirming submission — port 554 stayed "Connection refused" indefinitely. Broad port scan of .118 found ZERO open TCP ports while the device responded fine to ICMP.

Two confirmed reasons per Eufy's own docs + the Home Assistant community thread "Eufy camera RTSP stream is disabled after a few minutes":

1. The HomeBase doesn't run a persistent RTSP listener. Port 554 only binds when the camera is actively streaming (someone live-viewing in the app, or motion-triggered recording). When the camera is idle, the listener is closed. Hence "Connection refused" rather than timeout — the host actively replies "no service on this port."

2. Even when the listener IS up, the stream auto-disables after ~2-3 minutes of continuous streaming. To resume, the user must toggle RTSP off and back on in the Eufy app. This is intentional battery-preservation design — Eufy's RTSP feature is built for event-recording to a NAS (camera pushes when motion-triggered), not for continuous polling by a monitoring tool.

Workarounds the HA community uses (toggle-restart hacks, Continuous Recording mode, the `eufy_security` custom integration restarting streams every 2-3min) are too fragile for a tool meant to run unattended for weeks.

How to apply: For continuous-polling use cases (anything pulling a frame every N seconds for monitoring/alerting), do NOT use Eufy cameras regardless of model. Even Eufy's "supported RTSP" model list (eufyCam 2/2C/3/3C, Indoor Cam 2K, Solo IndoorCam C24, 2K PTZ) is for event recording, not monitoring. Recommend RTSP-native cameras with continuous listeners (Reolink, Amcrest, Dahua, Hikvision) instead.

Sources: Eufy "About NAS / RTSP" support article; HA Community thread "Eufy camera RTSP stream is disabled after a few minutes (my findings)"; bropat/eufy-security-ws issue #270.
